text_blocks.snippet: Yes, Agent Orange exposure is linked to an increased risk of lung cancer, particularly among Vietnam War veterans. The U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) recognizes respiratory cancers, including lung cancer, as presumptive conditions related to Agent Orange exposure. This means veterans diagnosed with lung cancer who served in Vietnam or other areas where Agent Orange was used are presumed to have developed the cancer due to their exposure and are eligible for VA benefits.
